chunks: (3) Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Mufadhdhal, Sa'dan ibn Ishaq ibn Sa'id, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qatawani all narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Hisham ibn Salim al-Jawaleeqi, from Yazeed al-Kinasi who said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) saying:
The master of this matter (al-Qa'im) has a likeness to Prophet Joseph; his mother is a black bondmaid. Allah will make his affairs succeed within a night.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: The Master of the Command (referring to the Mahdi)
key_terms.لَيْلَةٍ: A night (indicating a swift or specific timeframe for the event)
key_terms.يُوسُفَ: Joseph (Prophet Yusuf, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and characteristics of the Mahdi's mother and his rise according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) draws a parallel between the Mahdi and Prophet Joseph (Yusuf), specifically highlighting the unique detail of his mother being a bondmaid (Umm Walad), a detail often associated with the Prophet's lineage or the Mahdi's mother, Fatima al-Zahra. The phrase 'Allah will arrange his affair in a single night' (Yusuf's narrative of sudden elevation from prison to power) is interpreted by Shia scholars as a reference to the Mahdi's sudden reappearance (al-Zuhur) and the swift establishment of justice, mirroring the rapid transition in Yusuf's life. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions regarding the identity of the Mahdi's mother and the miraculous nature of his rise.
